ota.summary: # TubesZB 2026.10.29.1 This prerelease introduces a custom TubesZB web interface and one firmware per hardware model with saved DHCP/static IPv4 settings. ## Replacement for the failed 2026.10.29.0 build This prerelease supersedes [2026.10.29.0](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/releases/tag/2026.10.29.0), whose build stopped before compilation because the release version check imported Python `packaging`, which was unavailable in the ESPHome container. No firmware binaries or OTA feeds were published by that failed run. [Builder PR #201](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/pull/201) checks the version through the ESPHome CLI using Python's standard library. Every hardware config now reports `2026.10.29.1`. The firmware features and component PR #7 reference remain the same. Regression coverage includes running the guard without Python site-packages, supported/older compiler versions, prerelease boundaries, and malformed version output. All 40 Builder tests pass. A selective build of the 2026 Z-Wave profile also passed in the actual release container, including the version guard, compilation and firmware artifact upload. ## Important upgrade information **An existing firmware with a compiled-in static IP starts on DHCP on its first upgrade to this firmware.** The old compiled address is not present in the new settings storage. Find the device's DHCP lease in your router, or try its existing hostname. Open **Network**, enter the desired static settings, apply them, then open the new address and select **Keep settings** within two minutes. Update the connection address in ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT or Z-Wave JS if it changed. Once confirmed, network settings survive normal restarts and OTA updates that preserve NVS. An unconfirmed network trial automatically restores the previous configuration after 120 seconds or an unexpected reboot. Use the image for your exact hardware model. Use `.ota.bin` for a device OTA update and `.factory.bin` for a serial/USB installation with https://web.esphome.io. A factory installation may erase existing settings. Devices that have not previously been updated with ESP-IDF-based firmware may require a serial/USB update. ## New TubesZB interface The main device URL now opens a branded, self-contained management page with the TubesZB logo, desktop/mobile layouts and light/dark appearance. The interface is embedded in the firmware and does not require an internet-hosted frontend. - **Overview:** device identity, network and radio connection status. - **Zigbee / Z-Wave:** the controls and status supported by each radio, with independent sections on dual-radio hardware and a link from Zigbee to radio firmware controls. - **Network:** DHCP/static IPv4 configuration, validation of addresses and subnet settings, confirmation/rollback, and the saved **Use without internet** option. - **Firmware:** gateway and radio firmware management together, local OTA uploads, confirmation dialogs, progress at the top of the page and short completion messages. - **Diagnostics and logs:** a log dropdown on every section except Overview. Capture and history persist across navigation; returning to Overview hides the panel without discarding captured logs. Logs can be downloaded as text. Capture opens one shared event stream rather than a new stream per section. The original ESPHome interface remains at `/esphome` for compatibility. Existing ESPHome web-server authentication is honored when configured. ## Saved network settings and offline use Static entries are validated before saving, including IPv4 syntax, subnet mask and device/gateway consistency. A candidate configuration is staged and requires explicit confirmation at its new address; simply loading a page does not confirm a trial. **Use without internet** is saved across boots and restored before online checks begin. It disables connectivity/firmware-manifest checks and downloads while retaining local radio identity probes, serial traffic, the web UI and local OTA file uploads. Firmware pages show a link to the Builder's GitHub releases when this option is enabled. Re-enabling internet use starts a new connectivity check immediately. ## Radio firmware and controls - CC2652 flashing captures the existing Zigbee serial-server pause state, pauses it for programming, waits for the real native result and identity readback, then restores the prior state. It retains the readback delay even when a synchronous flash exceeds the queued-start timeout. A manually paused server stays paused. - Silicon Labs flashing supports the model-specific release feeds, direct custom HTTP(S) `.gbl` URLs, radio identity probing, reset and manual bootloader controls. Older models without a beta radio feed remain stable-only. - MGM21 dual-radio hardware uses native EZSP software bootloader entry because its boot pin is connected to an input-only ESP32 GPIO. The flasher requires the actual Gecko bootloader menu before transferring an image. Physical bootloader entry remains the recovery path for an unresponsive application. - Zigbee firmware manifests may specify an application `baudrate`. After a successful transfer, the flasher applies and saves it before releasing serial ownership. Failed transfers or missing metadata retain the previous rate; the bootloader's rate remains separate. A direct `.gbl` URL has no manifest baud metadata, so use the matching application baud when changing firmware that way. - Native callbacks provide flash progress and final results. Commands that never start recover instead of leaving controls locked indefinitely. Restart is available during recovery, while active firmware operations remain protected. On dual-radio devices, Zigbee maintenance uses the Zigbee UART/bridge. The shared ESP32 main loop can still delay Z-Wave traffic during maintenance; plan radio flashing accordingly. ## Hardware coverage The release builds 22 hardware profiles: | Family | Profiles | | --- | --- | | Single-radio CC2652 | CC2652P2 Ethernet/USB and PoE 2021–2023; CC2652P7 PoE 2023 | | Single-radio Silicon Labs | MGM24; MGM210 PoE 2022/2023; retired MGM12 Pro1 and original MGM210 Series 2 | | Dual-radio | CC2652 + Z-Wave, MGM24 + Z-Wave and MGM21 + Z-Wave, including their experimental entries | | Z-Wave | Original and 2026 Z-Wave profiles, including experimental entries | Newly enabled older-board flashing and MGM21 software entry still need physical-device verification. Earlier owner testing covered Z-Wave OTA/network rollback, CC2652 flash ownership, MGM24 + Z-Wave behavior, and BM24 forward/reverse baud migration between 115200 / 7.4.4.0 and 460800 / 9.1.2.1. These reports do not replace a final hardware pass for this version. ## Existing static-IP issue builds stay available The existing static-IP issue form and build action remain available during testing. They are isolated from this prerelease: - Builder source: previous published release `2026.10.25.0`, pinned to commit `7f968ca5aa95db46bd67e7be209946c45cb11bf5`. - ESPHome: `2026.6.5`, matching the prior successful release and issue builds. - Legacy components: pinned to `0e35b4afe1ad12b17418626d3bd75b7bcad52de6`. The form keeps its existing choices. The MGM21 “kit” choice maps to the released canonical filename, fixing the old mismatch. The action retains factory/OTA artifact downloads and its issue-comment link. It does not use the new runtime-network-settings wrappers or PR #7, and changes to the current release compiler variables cannot move its frozen compiler. Legacy templates retain their existing project-version labels. ## Build source and validation All 22 new product configs declare `2026.10.29.1` and require ESPHome `2026.10.1` or newer. New external components come from [esphome-components PR #7](https://github.com/tube0013/esphome-components/pull/7) through the shared `refs/pull/7/head` reference; the tested component snapshot is `18cac9ccfaf29dbf5bfe48a55f709c154b7727dd`. The Builder does not bundle local component copies. Keep the PR reference until the component changes are merged, then update the shared default deliberately. Validation covers the component host suite, configuration/release-isolation contracts, nine browser suites, all 22 new hardware builds and a serial-only compatibility build. The legacy path validates every form choice and compiles representative CC2652, MGM24 and Z-Wave images with its frozen compiler and components, including checks for both factory and OTA artifacts. The remaining radio API/interface refactor is a follow-up, not part of this testing release. It will consolidate check/probe status and direct operation calls while preserving the tested UART ownership and recovery behavior. Publishing this prerelease runs the beta build path (`Beta_Release` and `beta_ota_manifests`). Saving it as a draft does not publish firmware or change either OTA feed. Stable `Latest_Release` and `ota_manifests` remain on the existing release path. **Changes:** [Builder PR #200](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/pull/200) · [Component PR #7](https://github.com/tube0013/esphome-components/pull/7) · [Compare with 2026.10.25.0](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/compare/2026.10.25.0...2026.10.29.1)
